gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the makers' power ratings on the same footing. With the drives spun down, QNAP's own spec for the TS-464 (21.6 W, all bays filled) is about 9.3 W higher than Synology's for the DS925+ (12.33 W). That is roughly 81 kWh a year. KitGuru also measured the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus at 6.2 W more at idle when it is connected over its headline 10GbE port instead of 2.5GbE, so the 10GbE port costs about 54 kWh a year even when the box is doing nothing.
standout_why: Starry Hope's 4-bay page (cited 3 times) gives power figures, but each one comes from a different test: KitGuru's 24 W idle for the DXP4800 Plus with 4 HDDs, Dong Knows Tech's 30 W average for the DS925+, NASCompares' 13 W for the F4-425 Plus with 3 SSDs and no HDDs, and PCWorld's 25 W for the DXP4800 GT with drives asleep. It does not use maker figures for any model, has no hibernation-vs-access pair, and does not mention that the 10GbE link raises idle draw. nasdrives.ca (cited) has no power, noise or warranty figures at all. Our current page has no power column. I could not read thisping.com (TLS certificate error).
decides: This backs UGREEN as the hardware-value pick, with a footnote. Its 10GbE port is the main reason it beats the others, but using that port adds about 6 W at idle. For a home user on 2.5GbE, that extra draw is not there. The finding also counts against the QNAP TS-464 as the 'mature alternative'. On the makers' own figures it uses the most power with drives asleep, which is the state a home NAS spends most of its time in. The Synology DS925+ has the lowest maker-stated draw with drives spun down, which supports the 'stay with Synology for photos and backup' caveat.

findings.label: Maker power rating, access / HDD hibernation
findings.note: Same figures as the DS925neo+. The spec page points to a KB article for the test method but does not name the drives. I could not read that KB article's body (see unsourced).

findings.label: Maker noise rating and its test condition
findings.value: 20.5 dB(A), all bays filled with Synology SATA HDDs, idle
findings.note: Synology states the condition. QNAP's TS-464 spec page gives no dB figure, so noise cannot be compared using maker specs.

findings.label: M.2 storage pool on stock DSM
findings.value: Pools and cache need Synology-verified SSDs; listed models are SNV3410-400G, SNV5420-400G/800G/1600G
findings.note: Starry Hope already says the DS925+ M.2 slots take only Synology-listed NVMe, so this part is not new. What is new: the only listed drives are enterprise SSDs of 400 GB to 1.6 TB.

findings.label: Maker power rating, typical operation / disk standby
findings.value: 40.536 W operating (typical); 21.618 W disk standby; 'tested with drives fully populated'
findings.note: Drive model not stated. Compared with the DS925+ maker figures: standby 21.618 − 12.33 = 9.288 W, × 8,760 h = 81.4 kWh/yr more; operating 40.536 − 37.91 = 2.63 W more. The TS-464 has a 90 W adapter and max 16 GB RAM (QNAP modules only, per QNAP).

findings.label: M.2 interface
findings.note: One PCIe 3.0 lane per slot, about 1 GB/s each. The DXP4800 Plus slots are PCIe 4.0 (our current page; Starry Hope).

findings.label: Measured idle draw: 2.5GbE vs 10GbE link (KitGuru, Simon Crisp)
findings.value: 24.25 W idle on 2.5GbE; 30.45 W idle on 10GbE
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus 4-bay NAS Review (KitGuru), p.14
findings.note: Measured at the wall with WD Red WD60EFRX drives; KitGuru does not say how many. Review dated 2024-05-28. 30.45 − 24.25 = 6.2 W, × 8,760 h = 54.3 kWh/yr. No spun-down figure was reported.

findings.label: Measured load draw (KitGuru, Simon Crisp)
findings.value: Peak reads 52.07 W (2.5GbE) / 58.17 W (10GbE); peak writes 61.35 W (2.5GbE) / 67.02 W (10GbE)
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus 4-bay NAS Review (KitGuru), p.14
findings.note: This is a measured average during peak transfers, so it cannot be compared directly with Synology's or QNAP's 'access/typical' ratings.

findings.label: M.2 use on stock ADM
findings.value: SSD cache, separate storage pools, or a mix of both
findings.source_title: Asustor Lockerstor 4 Gen 2+ NAS Review (NAS Compares, 2026-02-27)
findings.note: NAS Compares lists 'NVMe drives as independent storage pools rather than cache only' as a pro and says the warranty stays valid with a third-party OS. Unlike Synology, no drive-vendor list is required.

findings.label: Maker power rating, operation / disk hibernation
findings.value: 25.1 W operation; 8.4 W disk hibernation; 19.7 dB (HDD idle); 3-year warranty
findings.note: The page has a footnote naming a test HDD (Seagate IronWolf 16TB ST16000VN001), but it is not clearly tied to the power figures, and the drive count is not given. The RAM is a fixed 2 GB, so this is an ARM-class low-power reference point, not a like-for-like pick.
